name: Topic 34: Dehydration signs and the urine-colour check
defaultTargetFormula: No new target. Use Topic 30 target_ml = base(sex: male 2500, female 2000, unknown 2500) + clamp((weight_kg - ref_weight) * 20, -400, 400) + min(workout_minutes * 8, 1000) + (hot_weather ? 500 : 0) + pregnancy/lactation adds; Topic 31 heat adds; clamp 1500-4500 ml; round to 50 ml. Urine-colour check: optional score 1-5 (1 almost clear; 2 pale straw; 3 light-mid yellow; 4 dark yellow or amber; 5 brown, orange-brown, red, pink or unsure); score 3 or 4 on two checks in a row adds one 250 ml prompt (est.), never above the 4500 ml cap; score 5 shows doctor note and no hydration tip. ICMR-NIN 2020 dehydration thresholds Not found.

drinks.name: Plain water
drinks.notes: Everyday drink; not enough alone for heavy diarrhoea

drinks.name: WHO/UNICEF reduced-osmolarity ORS
drinks.notes: 75 mmol/L sodium, 75 mmol/L glucose, 20 mmol/L potassium, 245 mOsm/L; for diarrhoea, vomiting or heat illness; made with stated water volume; not a daily drink

drinks.name: Home ORS (stop-gap)
drinks.notes: Half level teaspoon salt and 6 level teaspoons sugar per litre (secondary, unverified); only if no sachet

drinks.name: Sports or electrolyte drink
drinks.notes: About 18 mmol/L sodium, 6% carbohydrate (secondary); not a diarrhoea treatment

drinks.name: Tender coconut water
drinks.notes: About 6.6 mmol/L sodium, 50 mmol/L potassium (secondary, unverified); caution with potassium limits (Topic 19)

drinks.name: Chaas (salted)
drinks.notes: est.; sodium depends on salt added (Topic 18)

drinks.name: Packaged fruit juice
drinks.notes: est.; product policy; avoid in diarrhoea

drinks.name: Soft or cold drink (sugary)
drinks.notes: est.; product policy; avoid in diarrhoea

drinksTable.notes: 75 mmol/L Na (about 1,725 mg per litre, calc.), 75 mmol/L glucose (13.5 g/L), 20 mmol/L K, 245 mOsm/L

About 6.6 mmol/L Na, about 50.2 mmol/L K (Bell and Spriet; other sources differ, Topic 30); sugar not found
Not found (depends on salt added; see Topic 18)

reminderRules.rule: Optional urine-colour prompt at most twice a day; hidden for doctor-flag users
reminderRules.source: FitPlate design (est.); Armstrong 1994; Perrier 2017 (colour is a clue, not a test)

reminderRules.rule: Two urine scores of 3 or 4 in a row on a normal day add one 250 ml prompt, never beyond the 4500 ml cap
Urine score 5 (brown, orange-brown, red, pink, unsure) shows a doctor note and no hydration tip
reminderRules.source: NHS-derived haematuria guidance; MSD Manual (bilirubin) via search snippets (secondary)

reminderRules.rule: Any red flag tick (no urine 8 h or more, confusion, fainting, fast heartbeat, repeated vomiting or loose motions, infant or older adult unwell) shows 'Please speak to a doctor or call 112' and pauses prompts
reminderRules.source: NHS-derived dehydration pages; Irish HPSC infant guidance (8-12 h window; shorter used); WHO plans via MSF/NCBI

reminderRules.rule: Vomiting or loose motions logged: offer ORS quick-add (50-100 ml sips), continue food, ask a doctor about zinc for under-5s; adults on SGLT2 inhibitors, diuretics, metformin, ACE inhibitors or ARBs see 'ask your doctor'
reminderRules.source: WHO/UNICEF ORS statement; IAP/Indian Pediatrics 2010; UK sick-day leaflets via snippets (secondary)

reminderRules.rule: Users aged 60+: keep scheduled reminders even if not thirsty
reminderRules.source: Kenney and Chiu review (abstract only; secondary)

warnings: General information, not medical advice. The urine-colour check is a hydration nudge, not a diagnosis.
Red, pink, brown or cola-coloured urine not explained by food or a medicine needs a doctor, not more water.
No urine for 8 hours or more, confusion, fainting, fast heartbeat, repeated vomiting or diarrhoea, or any illness in a baby or older adult: seek medical help.
ORS is for illness, not for daily use. Use WHO-formula ORS made with the stated water volume; do not add extra salt.
Zinc for children with diarrhoea (10 mg/day under 6 months, 20 mg/day from 6 months, 10-14 days) is given on a doctor's advice.
Diuretics, SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, kidney, heart or liver disease and diabetes: follow your doctor's fluid and sick-day advice.
High thirst with frequent urination can signal high blood sugar: get tested.
ICMR-NIN 2020 dehydration thresholds Not found; all numeric thresholds here are secondary, unverified.
